project_info.* keys (D-025) are ProjectInformation-sourced identity items, additive to the pre-existing worksharing/version/build core -- see domains/identity.py's project_info field tables.

project_info.name/number/status/address/issue_date/client_name/building_name/organization_name/organization_description/ifc_building_guid/ifc_project_guid/ifc_site_guid are all Revit built-ins (BuiltInParameter), expected on every project (q=unreadable if the Parameter object itself is absent, not q=missing). The IFC GUID fields were originally implemented as shared/custom LookupParameter reads before a PR review follow-up confirmed via tools/archetype/bip_lookup.json that they are real BuiltInParameter members (IFC_BUILDING_GUID/IFC_PROJECT_GUID/IFC_SITE_GUID).

project_info.office is the only shared/custom field: Stantec's confirmed shared parameter (GUID 6b61afc7-13eb-4af5-8b65-889f978af4f3), read via Element.get_Parameter(Guid), legitimately absent on non-Stantec documents (q=unsupported.not_applicable, not q=unreadable).

Office's Address/City/State/Zip/Country/Telephone/Fax/Legal Entity sub-fields are deliberately NOT registered here -- their exact parameter names are unconfirmed against a real Stantec-template project (see CHANGELOG.md).

sig_hash_schema is pinned to identity.sig_hash.v2 (not the generator's default identity.sig_hash.v1) because D-025 changed the sig_hash preimage composition -- tools/generate_sig_hash_policy.py's build_policy() defaults any domain without this override to '<domain>.sig_hash.v1', which would silently erase the version bump on the next regeneration and make post-D-025 hashes appear compatible with the old preimage (PR review follow-up).
Records are emitted at family granularity (one record per Family element, not per FamilySymbol).
lft.family_name is label-only — excluded from identity_basis so sig_hash is name-independent.
lft.type_name removed: replaced by lft.type_count (count of collected types per family).
lft.family_symbol_count: API-reported total types; may differ from lft.type_count if types were filtered.
lft.type_parameter_schema_hash is the primary behavioral anchor for sig_hash.
lft.shape_gate.category_id is allowed but excluded from sig/join: Revit-version-specific int.
lft.family_is_editable and lft.family_is_in_place are discrimination signals (loaded vs system).
lft.structural_material_type is read from the family's representative FamilySymbol (Area 12 probe: constant across a family's types, unique_value_count=1 in every sampled case).

lft.is_active is a per-symbol (type) property, not per-family, and was observed to vary within a family in the Area 12 probe corpus; it is aggregated across all of a family's types to true/false/partial rather than read off a single arbitrary type, so the family record stays independent of collect_types() ordering.
sig_hash = f(category + schema_hash + is_in_place + is_editable + counts + structural_material_type + is_active).

sig_hash_schema is pinned to loaded_family_types.sig_hash.v2 (not the generator's default loaded_family_types.sig_hash.v1) because Area 12 changed the sig_hash preimage composition -- tools/generate_sig_hash_policy.py's build_policy() defaults any domain without this override to '<domain>.sig_hash.v1', which would silently erase the version bump on the next regeneration and make post-Area-12 hashes appear compatible with the old preimage (PR review follow-up, same precedent as the identity domain's D-025 sig_hash_schema pin above).
join_hash discovery: schema_hash is the behavioral anchor; individual parameter value items
(from parameter_rows) are future discovery work (see domain future-steps).
sig_hash basis: md5(material.name | material.class). Answers semantic identity.
join_hash basis: md5(material.graphics_sig_hash_v2 | material.keynote). Answers governance equivalence.
material.graphics_sig_hash_v2 retained as identity_item for visual consolidation analysis.
material.uid retained for record traceability only — not a sig or join anchor.
material.name_class_hash = md5(name | class), emitted by migration script and extractor.
material.manufacturer and material.model are allowed optional discovery candidates emitted by the migration script when present.
Subset policy decision: recognized exception; materials sig_hash and join_hash use intentionally disjoint preimages.

text_type.leader_arrowhead_sig_hash/_uid/_name are registered as allowed_keys (governed identity data, visible for join-key/pattern analysis) but deliberately excluded from sig_hash_keys: leader_arrowhead_uid is file-local (D-004 restricts UID use to element-backed identities), leader_arrowhead_name is cosmetic/presentation metadata, and promoting leader_arrowhead_sig_hash itself to hash-contributing is a separate future decision tied to the paused hash-composition discussion, not bundled into this registration change.

Without this sig_hash_keys override, tools/generate_sig_hash_policy.py would default the sig_hash preimage to every allowed_keys entry on the next policy regeneration, silently pulling the UID/name fields into text_types sig_hash and making identical text types hash differently purely due to per-file arrowhead UID/name — see core/sig_hash_builder.py's build_sig_hash_from_policy, which hashes every policy-allowed item, not just required_keys.
Domain family: view_category_overrides. Annotation category partition.
Cut properties not applicable to annotation categories — omitted from allowed_keys.

Both projection and cut properties applicable for model categories.
